standard.title: Technical Guidelines for Cosmetics and Personal Care Products

specification_sets.label: GU116 Annex 13 — General Safety Tests (all cosmetic and personal care products)
specification_sets.applies_to: All cosmetic and personal care products registered in Montaji. Toxic metal limits apply to the metals AS IMPURITIES, not as added ingredients.

limits.source_quote: Annex table, row 'Toxic Metals (Cadmium, Lead, Chromium, Arsenic, Mercury) / Note: as impurities / not added', Specification limit column: 'Cadmium 3ppm'. No comparison glyph is printed in the cell. Inclusivity taken from the governing sentence in section 6, page 12: 'Cosmetics shall: ... Not exceeding the limits for microbial contamination and toxic heavy metals as specified in Annex 1.' — a value equal to the limit is not exceeding it. Confidence medium rather than high because the cell itself carries no operator.
Annex table, Toxic Metals row: 'Lead 10ppm'. Inclusivity from section 6, page 12: 'Not exceeding the limits for microbial contamination and toxic heavy metals as specified in Annex 1.'
Annex table, Toxic Metals row: 'Arsenic 3 ppm'. Inclusivity from section 6, page 12: 'Not exceeding the limits for ... toxic heavy metals as specified in Annex 1.'
Annex table, Toxic Metals row: 'Mercury 3 ppm'. Inclusivity from section 6, page 12: 'Not exceeding the limits for ... toxic heavy metals as specified in Annex 1.'

Annex table, Toxic Metals row: 'Chromium (no standard)'. Chromium is named in the test description but DM states no limit for it, so no verdict can be rendered. Recorded explicitly so the resolver cannot silently pass a chromium result.
Annex table, row 'Asbestos', Specification limit: 'Absent - Not detected'. Non-detect requirement — never a numeric zero (migration 016).

Annex table, row 'Zinc', Specification limit: '1%'. AMBIGUOUS INCLUSIVITY — the cell prints a bare number with no glyph, and zinc is neither a 'toxic heavy metal' nor 'microbial contamination', so the section 6 governing sentence on page 12 does not reach it. Direction is taken as a maximum from the column header 'Specification limit' and section 6's 'Not contain any substance above the limit specified in the list of restricted substances'; the boundary itself is left null rather than guessed.
Annex table, row 'Free Formaldehyde', Specification limit: 'Absent - Not detected'.

Annex table, row 'Preservatives (Benzoic Acid, Methyl 4-Hydroxybenzoate, Ethyl 4-Hydroxybenzoate, n-Propyl 4-Hydroxybenzoate and n-Butyl 4-xybenzoate)', first line of Specification limit: '0.5% benzoic acid'. Bare number, no glyph; not covered by the page-12 'not exceeding' sentence (which names only heavy metals and microbial contamination). Inclusivity left null.
Annex table, Preservatives row: '0.4% Methyl Hydroxybenzoate (methylparaben)'. Bare number, no glyph — inclusivity null.
Annex table, Preservatives row: '0.4% Ethyl Hydroxybenzoate (ethylparaben)'. Bare number, no glyph — inclusivity null.
Annex table, Preservatives row: '0.4% Propyl Hydroxybenzoate (propylparaben)'. Bare number, no glyph — inclusivity null.
Annex table, Preservatives row: '0.4% Butyl Hydroxybenzoate (butylparaben)'. Bare number, no glyph — inclusivity null.

Annex table, Preservatives row, last line: '0.8%  Total Hydroxybenzoates'. A derived sum, not a directly measured analyte — the resolver must add the individual paraben results before judging. Bare number, no glyph — inclusivity null.

specification_sets.label: GU116 Annex 13 — Toxic metals in baby products, oral care and eye care (tighter limit)
specification_sets.applies_to: Baby products, oral care products, eye care products. AMBIGUOUS: the footnote does not say which of the five metals it replaces — see source_quote.
specification_sets.source_section: 13. Annex, Toxic Metals row, red footnote

limits.parameter_label: Toxic metals in baby / oral care / eye care products
limits.display: *For baby products, oral care, eye care up to 1 ppm
limits.source_quote: Annex table, Toxic Metals row, red footnote printed inside the Specification limit cell: '*For baby products, oral care, eye care up to 1 ppm'. TWO AMBIGUITIES, both left unresolved rather than guessed. (1) 'up to' is not a comparison operator — it does not settle whether exactly 1 ppm passes, so max_inclusive is null. (2) The footnote does not name a metal: it sits in the Toxic Metals cell and may mean each of Cd/Pb/As/Hg individually, or their sum, and it is not stated whether it also displaces the 10 ppm lead figure. A single parameter_key is used deliberately so that no per-metal verdict can be manufactured from it. DM would have to clarify before this row is sold.
Annex table, band 'Skin Whitening Products', row 'Hydroquinone', Specification limit: 'Absent'.

Annex table, band 'Skin Whitening Products', row 'Hydrogen Peroxide', Specification limit: 'Skin products: 4%'. Bare number, no glyph — inclusivity null. Note the same analyte carries three different limits in this document (4 % skin, 12 % hair and scalp, 0,1 %/6 % oral), so scope resolution is load-bearing here exactly as scoping doc section 7.4 warns.

specification_sets.label: GU116 Annex 13 — Hair and Scalp Products
specification_sets.source_section: 13. Annex, table band 'Hair and Scalp Products'

limits.source_quote: Annex table, band 'Hair and Scalp Products', row '1,4 Dioxane', Specification limit: '10 ppm'. Bare number, no glyph — inclusivity null.

limits.parameter_label: Hydrogen Peroxide in hair and scalp products
limits.source_quote: Annex table, band 'Hair and Scalp Products', row 'Hydrogen Peroxide', Specification limit: '12 %'. Bare number, no glyph — inclusivity null.

limits.parameter_label: Oxidative colorants (p-Phenylenediamine and its salts), concentration applied to hair after mixing
limits.display: After mixing under oxidative conditions the maximum concentration applied to hair must not exceed 2 % calculated as free base
limits.source_quote: Annex table, band 'Hair and Scalp Products', row 'Oxidatives Colorants (p-Phenylenediamine and its salts )': 'After mixing under oxidative conditions the maximum concentration applied to hair must not exceed 2 % calculated as free base'. INCLUSIVE on the explicit phrase 'must not exceed' — 2 % exactly does not exceed 2 %. Note the measurement basis: after mixing, as applied to hair, calculated as free base — not the concentration in the packaged product, so a certificate reporting the neat product is not judgeable against this row.

specification_sets.label: GU116 Annex 13 — Oral Hygiene Products
specification_sets.applies_to: Oral hygiene products (mouth rinse, toothpaste); the hydrogen peroxide row splits out tooth whitening/bleaching products.

limits.source_quote: Annex table, band 'Oral Hygiene Products', row 'Total Fluoride', Specification limit: '0.15%'. Bare number, no glyph — inclusivity null. Section 9.6 (page 18) makes the test mandatory where a fluoride compound is on the label: 'the applicant/ manufacturer should provide total fluoride content by testing in Dubai central lab or any accredited laboratories.'
Annex table, band 'Oral Hygiene Products', row 'Di-ethylene Glycol', Specification limit: 'Absent'.

limits.parameter_label: Hydrogen Peroxide in oral products (mouth rinse, toothpaste, tooth whitening/bleaching)
limits.display: Oral products, including mouth rinse, toothpaste and tooth whitening or bleaching products: ≤ 0,1 %
limits.source_quote: Annex table, band 'Oral Hygiene Products', row 'Hydrogen Peroxide': 'Oral products, including mouth rinse, toothpaste and tooth whitening or bleaching products: ≤ 0,1 %'. INCLUSIVE on the printed ≤ glyph, verified on the rendered page. European decimal comma in the source.

limits.parameter_label: Hydrogen Peroxide in tooth whitening or bleaching products (professional band)
limits.display: *Specific for Tooth whitening or bleaching products: > 0,1 % ≤ 6 %
limits.source_quote: Annex table, band 'Oral Hygiene Products', row 'Hydrogen Peroxide', starred sub-clause: '*Specific for Tooth whitening or bleaching products: > 0,1 % ≤ 6 % / *not allowed under 18 years / *first use by dental practitioners'. Lower bound EXCLUSIVE on the printed > glyph, upper bound INCLUSIVE on the printed ≤ glyph; both verified on the rendered page. This is a permitted band, not a pass/fail range: a tooth whitening product at or below 0,1 % falls under the preceding row instead, and this band additionally carries two non-numeric conditions (not for under-18s, first use by a dental practitioner) that no laboratory certificate can evidence.

specification_sets.label: GU116 Annex 13 — Lard in Cosmetics (lip products, creams & soap)
specification_sets.source_section: 13. Annex, table band 'Lard in Cosmetics (Lips products, creams & soap)'

limits.source_quote: Annex table, band 'Lard in Cosmetics (Lips products, creams & soap)', row 'Analysis of Lard', Specification limit: 'Absent'.

specification_sets.label: GU116 Annex 13 — Perfumes, Toilet Waters, Eau de Cologne, cosmetic product
specification_sets.applies_to: Perfumes, toilet waters, eau de cologne and cosmetic products.
specification_sets.source_section: 13. Annex, table band 'Perfumes , Toilet Waters, Eau de Cologne, cosmetic product'

limits.display: Allergens equal to or above the below limits should be indicated on the label (within the ingredients) as follow: - 0,001 % in leave-on products (e.g.: perfumes / lotion, cream) - 0,01 % in rinse-off products (e.g., shampoo, conditioner)
limits.source_quote: Annex table, band 'Perfumes , Toilet Waters, Eau de Cologne, cosmetic product', row 'Allergens'. DELIBERATELY UNBOUNDED: 'equal to or above the below limits should be indicated on the label' is a LABELLING trigger, not a pass/fail limit — exceeding 0,001 % does not make the product non-compliant, it makes the allergen declarable. Encoding it as a bound would produce a false NON-COMPLIANT. Numbers preserved verbatim in display only. Same wording as GU117 Table 1 (page 11 of that document), except GU116 omits GU117's leading 'No maximum limit:'.
Annex table, band 'Perfumes , Toilet Waters, Eau de Cologne, cosmetic product', row 'Methanol', Specification limit: 'Absent'.

specification_sets.label: GU116 Annex 13 — Microbiology Tests
specification_sets.applies_to: All cosmetic and personal care products; the two enumeration rows carry a tighter limit for baby products.

limits.source_quote: Annex table, band 'Microbiology Tests', row 'Enumeration of Aerobic Mesophilic bacteria (Total bacterial count)', Specification limit: '< 1000 CFU/g'. EXCLUSIVE on the printed < glyph, verified on the rendered page — a result of exactly 1000 CFU/g fails. NOTE THE CONFLICT: section 6 on page 12 says cosmetics shall be 'Not exceeding the limits for microbial contamination ... as specified in Annex 1', which reads inclusive, while the Annex prints an exclusive <. The glyph in the limit cell governs (rule 1); the tension is recorded here rather than resolved silently.

limits.parameter_label: Aerobic Mesophilic bacteria (Total bacterial count) — baby products
limits.source_quote: Annex table, band 'Microbiology Tests', row 'Enumeration of Aerobic Mesophilic bacteria', second line printed in red: 'Baby products: < 100 CFU/g'. EXCLUSIVE on the printed < glyph.
Annex table, band 'Microbiology Tests', row 'Detection of Detection of Escherichia coli (E-Coli) Escherichia coli' (the duplicated wording is as printed), Specification limit: 'All products: Absent'.
Annex table, band 'Microbiology Tests', row 'Detection of Staphylococcus aureus', Specification limit: 'All products: Absent'.
Annex table, band 'Microbiology Tests', row 'Detection of Pseudomonas aeruginosa', Specification limit: 'All products: Absent'.
Annex table, band 'Microbiology Tests', row 'Detection of Candida albicans', Specification limit: 'All products: Absent'.
Annex table, band 'Microbiology Tests', row 'Enumeration of Yeast & Mould', Specification limit: '< 1000 CFU/g'. EXCLUSIVE on the printed < glyph.
Annex table, band 'Microbiology Tests', row 'Enumeration of Yeast & Mould', second line printed in red: 'Baby products: < 100 CFU/g'. EXCLUSIVE on the printed < glyph.

specification_sets.label: GU116 9.6 Special cases — Alpha-hydroxy-acid (skin peeling) products
specification_sets.applies_to: Cosmetic products containing alpha-hydroxy acids (citric, glycolic, lactic, malic, mandelic, tartaric acid etc.). Two different limits by intended user: retail vs professional-only.

limits.parameter_label: pH of the final product (retail use)
limits.display: The final product has a pH of 3.5 or greater (retail use)
limits.source_quote: Section 9.6, page 19: 'the applied product must comply with the following criteria: - The final product has a pH of 3.5 or greater (retail use) & pH of 3 or greater (professional use ONLY)'. INCLUSIVE — '3.5 or greater' explicitly includes 3.5. This is a MINIMUM, not a maximum: an acidic product below pH 3.5 fails.

limits.parameter_label: pH of the final product (professional use only)
limits.display: pH of 3 or greater (professional use ONLY)
limits.source_quote: Section 9.6, page 19: '... & pH of 3 or greater (professional use ONLY)'. INCLUSIVE — '3 or greater' includes 3. Applying the professional limit to a retail product would pass a product DM would fail, which is precisely the scope-resolution hazard of scoping doc section 7.4.

obligations.cadence_note: No cadence. The laboratory test report is a product-dossier document for registration; registration then runs 5 years (8.5). Not a periodic sampling programme.
obligations.trigger_event: application to register a cosmetic or personal care product in Montaji (and at 5-year renewal)
obligations.applies_to: Importers, local manufacturers, and agents of foreign manufacturers — 'Individuals who import or locally manufacture Cosmetic products & Personal care, or have products imported or manufactured on their behalf are responsible for applying to have their products registered' (8.1, page 15).
obligations.source_quote: Page 18, 9.4: 'A document to declare in details the result of laboratory test for Cosmetic product. This report needs to be issued by a certified lab and accredited test methods. A detailed list of laboratory tests will be listed in Annex 1.' Page 22: 'In order to ensure the compliance of each product to the recommended limits by Dubai Municipality, products should be tested at Dubai Central Laboratory or any other accredited laboratory.'

obligations.trigger_event: product label lists a fluoride compound as an ingredient
obligations.source_quote: Page 18, 9.6: 'If the product label listed a form of fluoride as an ingredient ... then the applicant/ manufacturer should provide total fluoride content by testing in Dubai central lab or any accredited laboratories.'

obligations.trigger_event: manufacture, import, export, advertisement, sale or distribution of a cosmetic product in Dubai; and registration must precede import
obligations.source_quote: Page 14, section 8: 'no Cosmetic product shall be manufactured, imported, exported, advertised, sold or distributed in Dubai unless it has been registered in Montaji system'. Page 19, section 10: 'Cosmetic categories shall be registered prior to import or export process'.

obligations.cadence_note: DM-side establishment inspection programme. NO frequency is published in this document — the cadence is the regulator's, not the regulated party's, and it cannot be turned into a due date for a client.
obligations.applies_to: Establishments trading or promoting cosmetics in the Dubai market (inspected BY Dubai Municipality)
obligations.source_quote: Page 19, 11.1: 'Market compliance assured by establishments' inspection program covers the following: Status of product registration; Physical conformity of products; Sampling for related laboratory testing'. This is the one genuinely recurring activity in the document, and it is DM's own — the trader cannot schedule it.

obligations.cadence_note: Certificates must be VALID AT THE TIME OF SUBMISSION — an expiry-driven condition, closest in shape to the section 4.4 certificates primitive.
obligations.applies_to: Local manufacturer (GMP ISO 22716); country-of-origin authority (Free Sale Certificate); Islamic society (HALAL, if the logo is used)
obligations.source_quote: Page 17, 9.3: 'This certificate is requested for local manufacturer; must be issued from certified bodies and needs to be valid at the time of submission.' Page 17, 9.1 (FSC): 'should be valid at the time of submission and request.' Page 18, 9.5: 'HALAL certificate ... needs to be valid at the time of submission.'

obligations.trigger_event: any subsequent amendment in the particulars of the registration
obligations.source_quote: Page 16, 8.4: 'After a Cosmetic Product has been registered, any subsequent amendment in particulars of the application relating to the Cosmetic product must be notified or approved by the Registration and Permits Section.'

obligations.trigger_event: product does not comply with health and safety requirements, or DM/another authority requests a recall
obligations.source_quote: Page 20, 11.3: 'The product recall & withdrawal is promptly and efficiently retrieving Batch/ Bar Code of the product that does not comply with health and safety requirements, or that may have an undesirable effect on consumers.'

extraction_notes.render_verified: Annex pages 22 and 23 were rendered at 200 dpi and read as images. Every inclusivity call above was taken from the glyph visible in the rendered cell, not from text extraction ordering.
extraction_notes.limits_called_recommended: Page 22 opens the Annex with 'the recommended limits by Dubai Municipality'. 'Recommended' sits awkwardly against section 6's mandatory 'Cosmetics shall: ... Not exceeding the limits ... as specified in Annex 1' (page 12). Section 6 is the operative sentence and is what makes this module_kind 'compliance'; the word 'recommended' should be flagged before a report asserts NON-COMPLIANT on an Annex row alone.
extraction_notes.limits_declared_volatile: Page 24: 'All the specification limit should be updated/revised as per the update in the regulation/standard' and 'Cosmetic & personal care product may be subjected for further chemical testing as per the scope of application'. The published table is therefore neither closed nor self-dating.
extraction_notes.laboratory: 'Dubai Central Laboratory or any other accredited laboratory' (page 22) and 'a certified lab and accredited test methods' (page 18). As with GU117, this is a far wider laboratory universe than the DM-accredited closed set the FM modules rely on (decision 8).
extraction_notes.applies_to_scope_problem: 'consumer_product' is NOT a permitted value under migration 022, which allows only 'lagoon' and 'facilities'. Every specification_set above will fail that CHECK as written. See consumer_products_notes.md.
extraction_notes.version_provenance: V 2.1, issue date 15th Sept 2025, superseding 4th May 2024 — from the cover (page 1), the Document History Log (page 2) and every page footer. The catalogue's portal_document_date is 2026-01-30 and the upload path is /uploads/2026/01/; neither is the issue date. The code prints with an internal space, 'DM-HSD- GU116-CPCP2', on every page — recorded as printed, per the section 7.12 warning that codes are not uniform.
